messages.author: f2659346bc7923d6
messages.subject: SEM multigroup - non normal data
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to do a multigroup SEM with a non normal data set.
I have received the following output: 

Error in if (fx < 0) fx <- 0 : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing,  :
  lavaan WARNING sample covariance can not be inverted in group: 1
2: In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing,  :
  lavaan WARNING sample covariance can not be inverted in group: 2
3: In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing,  :
  lavaan WARNING: number of observations (205) too small to compute Gamma in group: 2

I did not understand what it means.

I would be glad with any insight.

Best regards,
Vinícius

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: SEM multigroup - non normal data
parts:
On 05/28/2015 02:32 PM, Vinícius Lionel Mateus wrote:
> 1: In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing, :
> lavaan WARNING sample covariance can not be inverted in group: 1

Well, this is your problem (the first of many): the sample covariance
matrix of your observed variables for the first group can not be
inverted. This means the covariance matrix is singular. Maybe, some
variables are a linear combination of other variables?

> 2: In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing, :
> lavaan WARNING sample covariance can not be inverted in group: 2

> 3: In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing, :
> lavaan WARNING: number of observations (205) too small to compute Gamma in group: 2

It would seem you have a fairly large model, and your sample size in
group 2 (N=205) is way too small to get a reliable estimate of the
weight matrix. Using non-normal corrections may not be feasible for your
sample.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: SEM multigroup - non normal data
parts:

I have used the same approach to other variables in the model.
